title: Influence without authority, including senior leaders
summary: PMs rarely manage the people they work with. You get things done by building trust, using evidence and understanding what others care about.

beginner: Learn what each key person cares about and how they are measured.
Build trust by doing what you say and sharing credit.
Talk to people one to one before big meetings.
When you disagree, say so early and calmly, with a proposal.
Ask for feedback on how you come across.
experienced: Frame proposals in terms of leaders' goals.
Escalate with options and a recommendation.
Build a network across the organisation before you need it.

toolExamples.notion: Keep notes on each stakeholder's goals and concerns.
toolExamples.claude: Describe a tough conversation and ask it to role-play the other person so you can practise.

pitfalls: Relying on the strength of your argument alone
